question: With the same required native replace_line tool and 96-token cap, does returning a bounded host rejection reason instead of the generic unknown-tool result improve independently scored delivery by t=395 s?

source.failure: Both arms run the same comment-stripped program and receive the identical trusted five-line excerpt around the line-81 TypeError.

timing.dispatch_validity: The scripted first reply must finish within 2 s of t=250 and the first live repair request must start within 5 s after release. Freeze actual files once at t=395.

split.unit: Two unseen inputs reproduce one fixed real-model defect. Results estimate conditional recovery, not official PLE score.

design.baseline: native-patch: expose only replace_line(line, replacement), set tool_choice=required and max_tokens=96. A rejected call is returned unchanged to the general harness, which produces its existing unknown-tool result.
design.candidate: native-feedback: use the identical tool, schema, guard and cap. For one registered replace_line call rejected by the guard, append the original assistant tool call plus exactly one tool result containing only accepted=false and the registered reason code, then make one immediate retry in the same model conversation. Accepted calls and unregistered call shapes follow the baseline path.
design.single_changed_module: Host rejection acknowledgement: generic unknown-tool result versus one bounded, schema-independent reason code in the actual tool-result channel. Source, tool schema, host acceptance rules, transformed program, model, sampling, timing, execution and scoring are shared.
design.model: google-cloud/gemma-4-26b through the pinned local Gemma 4 26B A4B GGUF runner
design.evaluation: Primary outcome is normalized independent file score at t=395 and candidate-minus-baseline paired difference. Report all 12 scores, per-case mean differences, each repeat's cross-case macro difference, grand paired mean and n-1 sample variance. Also report exact request-shape compliance, rejection feedback exposure, reason codes, repeated-patch rate, host acceptance/execution and first executable-patch latency.
design.decision: Require six complete pairs, correct source exposure in all 12 arms, identical registered native tool requests in all 12 arms, candidate rejection feedback observed in all six candidate arms and absent in all six baselines, and production-wrapper positive and negative controls. Continue only if all three repeat macro differences are strictly positive and neither N nor O has a negative mean difference. Stop the feedback module if complete coverage fails the score gate. Rerun only an entire technically invalid pair and preserve the first valid pair.
design.attempts: Archive every attempt and reason. Never rerun a valid low score. Use the first complete valid pair in time order.

feedback_contract.no_solution_leakage: The feedback contains no source text, correct replacement, variable name, target cost, score, output, or execution result.

guard_controls.positive: An already valid replacement is converted directly to one run_python call in both arms without feedback. An indented registered replacement receives exactly one bounded tool result in the candidate; a valid retry is converted to run_python and scores 1 with costs 57 and 67 on N/O.
negative: feedback containing source or a replacement
guard_controls.request_lock: All live repair requests in both arms contain exactly one function named replace_line, tool_choice required, no general tools and max_tokens 96. Only candidate retry requests contain the registered tool-result payload.

inherits.implementation_lock: Commit runner, feedback wrapper, recorder, workflow, input fixtures and protocol before inference; record immutable experiment SHA, run and jobs. Run transport, request-shape, no-leakage and production-wrapper positive and negative controls before model startup.
